title: Runflow Steward: taskifier and contextual admin utility for safe remediations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a lightweight Runflow Steward service and CLI that converts canonical runbook steps into idempotent, auditable tasklets and exposes a contextual admin utility for on-call and first-line support. Goals: 1) reduce manual playbook error-rate by >40% for common incidents, 2) enable dry-run and staged canary execution for sensitive remediations, 3) emit structured telemetry that ties runbook steps to quality/regression alerts in Optimize. Scope: runbooks-as-tasks translator, short-lived execution sandbox (ephemeral credentials), CLI/console surface for parameterized runs, Telemetry schema, RBAC gating. Out of scope for this ticket: long-running multi-step orchestration (will be separate), multi-tenant private deployment packaging.

acceptance_criteria: CLI/console can convert a canonical runbook (Confluence format) into a tasklet bundle with parameter schema
Dry-run mode executes in sandbox and returns deterministic preview logs without mutating production state
Execution path emits structured telemetry (trace id, step id, result codes) to Grafana/Traces and links back to runbook URL
RBAC gating enforced: only roles with 'runflow.execute' can perform non-dry runs; KMS-integrated ephemeral creds used for privileged ops
Automated idempotency test harness passes (no duplicate side effects when replaying same idempotencyKey)
implementation_steps: Format parser: Confluence->canonical AST (2d spike) - done
Tasklet schema design and proto definition (idempotencyKey, paramSpec, guard checks) - complete
Sandbox executor: implement short-lived credentials, namespace isolation, and dry-run mode (4d)
CLI/console integration: parameterized run form, preview, and telemetry link (3d)
Telemetry: instrument step start/end/result and integrate with existing tracing pipeline (2d) - partial
Security: integrate KMS and rotate ephemeral creds; complete security checklist and threat model (2d)
QA: expand idempotency harness and run chaos scenarios (3d)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental production mutation from insufficient sandboxing. Mitigation: default to dry-run for new runflows and require explicit 'approve' with SSO reauth for live runs.

Risk: idempotency boundaries unclear for steps that modify external systems. Mitigation: enforce explicit compensation and post-check contracts in paramSpec; mark high-risk steps in console with red warning.
Risk: telemetry volume could spike. Mitigation: sampling + adaptive aggregation; provide toggle per-project to adjust retention.
Risk: security approval slowdowns. Mitigation: early engagement with SecOps and provide a hardened minimal SRE path for urgent incident escalations.
